react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on two biological domains disrupted by the treatment. The strongest cross-paradigm signal is **one-carbon metabolism centred on glycine, serine and threonine metabolism** (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260). RaMP ORA ranks this KEGG map top overall (FDR 3.1e-16, fold-enrichment 663, 7 metabolites hit: choline, O-phospho-L-serine, sarcosine, AMP, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, (R)-lipoic acid, L-cystathionine). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently places 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' as rank-1 pathway (p=0.019, 8 compounds overlapping — full input set mapped through the mfn empirical network). MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG-namespace) nominates hsa00270 'Cysteine and methionine metabolism' as its top significant hit (p=0.0009, 3 metabolites: SAM, L-cystathionine, O-phospho-L-serine) and hsa00260 as rank-2. The WikiPathways hit WP:WP2525 'Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways' (FDR 8.8e-14) bridges the one-carbon and trans-sulfuration branches, with 6 of the input metabolites confirmed present (choline, phosphoserine, sarcosine, phosphorylcholine, SAM, L-cystathionine). A secondary coordinated hit is **glycerophospholipid metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00564), confirmed by RaMP and MetaboAnalystR (phosphorylcholine + choline, p=0.02), consistent with mummichog's rank-2 'Glycerophospholipid metabolism'. Driver metabolites span two functional poles: (i) the one-carbon node — SAM (KEGG:C00019), choline (C00114), phosphoserine (C01005) and sarcosine (C00213) — and (ii) the lipid-signalling node — phosphorylcholine (C00588) and choline (C00114). The trans-sulfuration intermediates lipoic acid (C16241) and L-cystathionine (C02291) link the one-carbon and hydrogen-sulfide generation arms. Biocytin (C05552), AMP (C00020), UMP (C00105) and cholesterol (C00187) appear as pathway periphery hits consistent with broader cellular-energy and membrane-remodelling disturbances but do not drive the top-ranking enrichment.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on two biological domains disrupted by the treatment. The strongest cross-paradigm signal is **one-carbon metabolism centred on glycine, serine and threonine metabolism** (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260). RaMP ORA ranks this KEGG map top overall (FDR 3.1e-16, fold-enrichment 663, 7 metabolites hit: choline, O-phospho-L-serine, sarcosine, AMP, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, (R)-lipoic acid, L-cystathionine). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently places 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' as rank-1 pathway (p=0.019, 8 compounds overlapping — full input set mapped through the mfn empirical network). MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG-namespace) nominates hsa00270 'Cysteine and methionine metabolism' as its top significant hit (p=0.0009, 3 metabolites: SAM, L-cystathionine, O-phospho-L-serine) and hsa00260 as rank-2. The WikiPathways hit WP:WP2525 'Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways' (FDR 8.8e-14) bridges the one-carbon and trans-sulfuration branches, with 6 of the input metabolites confirmed present (choline, phosphoserine, sarcosine, phosphorylcholine, SAM, L-cystathionine). A secondary coordinated hit is **glycerophospholipid metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00564), confirmed by RaMP and MetaboAnalystR (phosphorylcholine + choline, p=0.02), consistent with mummichog's rank-2 'Glycerophospholipid metabolism'. Driver metabolites span two functional poles: (i) the one-carbon node — SAM (KEGG:C00019), choline (C00114), phosphoserine (C01005) and sarcosine (C00213) — and (ii) the lipid-signalling node — phosphorylcholine (C00588) and choline (C00114). The trans-sulfuration intermediates lipoic acid (C16241) and L-cystathionine (C02291) link the one-carbon and hydrogen-sulfide generation arms. Biocytin (C05552), AMP (C00020), UMP (C00105) and cholesterol (C00187) appear as pathway periphery hits consistent with broader cellular-energy and membrane-remodelling disturbances but do not drive the top-ranking enrichment.
